name: Forts and Castles, Volta, Greater Accra, Central and Western Regions
description: Strung along Ghana's coast between Keta and Beyin, these whitewashed forts and castles were built between 1482 and 1786 as trading posts, first by the Portuguese and later by other European powers. Elmina Castle, founded in 1482, is the oldest surviving European building in Sub-Saharan Africa. Its walls, which first served the gold trade, later held enslaved people awaiting shipment across the Atlantic.
